lead_time.formula: Lead time is the supplied lead_time in days. Bands: 0-7, 8-30, 31-90 and 91+ days. A band figure is the records in the band over the records of its group. The median is the middle value of the lead times of the group (the mean of the two middle values when the count is even). A group figure is the records of the group over all records with a lead time.
limitations: Records without a lead time are left out and counted in records_without_lead_time.
The supplied lead time is used as it is; it is not checked against the booking date.
The analysis describes how far ahead guests book; it does not say why.

holidays.formula: A day group is the holiday days of the calendar, or the non-holiday days within 1, 3 or 7 days before or after a holiday. Its figure is the bookings (or arrivals) on those days over the number of those days in the span of the data, zero-booking days included; mean_per_day is that ratio. The baseline is the days of the span that are neither holiday nor in the group and fall on a weekday that the group has. cancellation_share (arrivals only) is the cancelled arrivals of the group over its arrivals.
limitations: The span is from the first to the last date in the data; days outside the years of the holiday calendar are left out and the years are listed in years_unavailable.
A difference between holiday days and the baseline is an association, not a cause.
Holidays in other countries, school holidays and events are not in the calendar.
Records without the date are left out and counted.

findings.note: Holiday figures describe associations between dates and activity; other factors are not adjusted for. Days in years the holiday calendar does not cover are left out.

seasonality.formula: Bookings are counted by booking date and arrivals by arrival date, per calendar month and per ISO week. A period figure is the records in the period over all records with the date. cancellation is the cancelled records of the period over its records. mean_price_per_night is the mean of price_per_night over the records of the period that have a price.
limitations: A period is partial when the data starts after its first day or ends before its last day; compare partial periods with care.
Only periods with at least one record are listed.
A year with fewer than 12 months of data is listed in incomplete_years; a seasonal pattern needs complete years.
Records without the date are left out and counted.
The mean price is a mean of prices per night, not weighted by nights.

findings.note: Bookings are counted by booking date and arrivals by arrival date, as separate series. Figures describe observed counts per period; no seasons are defined, and a partial period is not fully covered by the observed dates.

bookings.summary: 5000 bookings were observed from 2016-06-24 to 2019-04-11, in 25 months and 81 ISO weeks; 4 of these periods are partial. This describes the observed data only.

arrivals.summary: 5000 arrivals were observed from 2018-07-01 to 2019-04-11, in 10 months and 42 ISO weeks; 3 of these periods are partial. This describes the observed data only.

cancellations.formula: The cancellation share of a group is the cancelled bookings of the group over all its bookings. Lead time bands are 0-7, 8-30, 31-90 and 91+ days.
limitations: A share is an observed association between a booking trait and cancellation, not a cause.
Bookings that lack the trait of a split are left out of that split and counted in records_left_out.
The groups of a split are not independent of each other (a long lead time is more common in some market segments).
Whether a booking was cancelled is as the data says; no cancellation date is known.

findings.note: Cancellation shares are observed associations between a booking attribute and cancellation status; other factors are not adjusted for, and nothing is predicted.

room_value.formula: Length of stay is the weekend nights plus the week nights. The buckets are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5-7 and 8+ nights; a bucket figure is the records in it over the records with at least one night. The estimated value of a booking is price_per_night times nights, in the price units of the input; total is the sum and mean the mean over the bookings that have a price.
limitations: The estimated value is an ESTIMATE, not revenue: taxes, fees, discounts, extras, the currency and what a cancelled guest paid are not known.
Bookings of no nights are left out and counted in zero_night_records.
Bookings without a price are left out of the value and counted; a price of zero is included and counted in zero_price_records.
Cancelled bookings are valued like the others, so the value of cancelled bookings is not money lost.

estimate.label: Estimate in the price units of the input: price per night times nights. It is not revenue.

estimated_value.label: Estimate in the price units of the input: price per night times nights. It is not revenue.

overall.summary: Estimated value of 4930 bookings in group 'all': total 0, no mean (no booking has a price) in the price units of the input (an estimate, not realized revenue).

guest_mix.formula: A distribution figure is the bookings with the trait value over all bookings that have the trait. For each value: mean_length_of_stay is the mean nights, cancellation_share the cancelled bookings over the bookings of the value, mean_price_per_night the mean price per night of the bookings that have a price. Total guests is adults plus children plus babies.
limitations: Bookings that lack a trait are left out of its distribution and counted in records_left_out.
A difference between values is an association; the values differ in other traits too.
A value with fewer than 30 bookings is flagged small_sample and its means are unreliable.
Total guests counts a missing adults, children or babies value as zero when another of the three is known.

findings.note: Distributions show how bookings are spread over each attribute. A comparison is stated only for groups that are not small samples; it describes an observed association only.

occupancy.formula: Occupancy is the room nights taken over room_count times the nights of the period. A room night is taken from the arrival to the day before the departure (arrival plus nights, minus one day); only nights inside the period count. Cancelled bookings take no room night. The period is the given one, or from the first arrival to the last night taken.
limitations: room_count is the number of rooms the caller gives; rooms that are closed or out of order are not known.
Cancelled bookings are taken as empty rooms; a no-show or a late cancellation that was paid is not known.
A booking of no nights takes no room night.
Nothing is capped: a share above 100 % means the bookings hold more room nights than room_count rooms can, for example overbooking or a room_count that is too low.
Bookings that start before the period or end after it count only inside it; a period shorter than the bookings' span ignores the rest of them.
On 11 day(s) of the period the room nights taken exceeded room_count; the shares are not capped and can be above 100 %.

findings.summary: Occupancy was 40.4 % (12112 of 30000 room nights) from 2018-07-01 to 2019-04-26.

occupancy_on_holidays.formula: Occupancy is the room nights taken over room_count times the number of days. The holiday days figure uses the days of the period that are holidays in the calendar, the other days figure the remaining days of the period. A room night is taken from the arrival to the day before the departure; cancelled bookings take none.
limitations: Days in years that the holiday calendar does not cover are left out of both figures and counted in days_left_out_unavailable_years.
The difference between holiday days and other days is an association; weekends, seasons and events fall on holidays too.
A holiday that falls in a short period gives a small sample.
Nothing is capped: a share above 100 % means more room nights than room_count rooms.
Cancelled bookings are taken as empty rooms.

findings.summary: Occupancy was 27.9 % on holiday days and 40.7 % on other days from 2018-07-01 to 2019-04-26; this is an observed association only.

correlations.formula: Spearman rank correlation: the Pearson correlation of the ranks of two fields, with tied values given the mean of their ranks. A pair uses the bookings that have both values. is_canceled is 1 for a cancelled booking and 0 otherwise. The value is between -1 and 1, or null when a field is constant in the pair or fewer than 2 bookings have both values.
limitations: A correlation shows that two fields move together; it does not show that one causes the other.
Spearman finds a steady rise or fall, not other shapes of relation.
A value is null when it cannot be calculated; bookings with a missing value are left out of each pair, so pairs rest on different bookings (see records_used).
Fields that are text or flags other than is_canceled are not in the matrix.

findings.summary: Spearman rank correlation between 12 fields, each pair over the bookings that have both values; a correlation is not a cause.
